title: Latency + Failure Journey Playbook and Sketch Notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook + quick wireframe writeup for a compact console surface that helps engineers triage request failures driven by latency/timeouts, 5xx responses, and model-level errors (e.g., OOM, tokenization failures, invalid logits). Goal: reduce mean time to root cause by providing a small set of high-value snapshots and one-click actions that are cheap to implement and easy to iterate on.

Audience:
- Platform/infra SREs doing first-pass incident triage
- Model-onboarding engineers debugging model rejection modes
- Product/support engineers investigating customer reported high latencies or error spikes

Problem framing (short):
- Current console pages are dense and require clicking across logs, call traces, and model debug pages.
- Common pain: "I see too many 5xx spikes but no idea which model variant or routing policy caused it."
- Timeouts are often confused with slow model cold starts, batch contention, or upstream network issues.

Design constraints:
- Must render in under 150ms for SRE console (no heavy re-computation in UI).
- Prefer server-side precomputed aggregates for the last 30m/1h windows; allow detail fetch on demand (replay / timeline).
- Reuse existing trace and logs infra (no new telemetry pipeline).
- Must work whether hosted/dedicated/private.

Core UX surfaces proposed (high level):
1) Failure Journey Matrix (top-left):
   - 2D grid: X axis = failure class (Timeout / 5xx / ModelError / Mismatch), Y axis = latency bucket (fast/median/slower).
   - Each cell shows: count, sample rate, and % of requests with prefix cache hits.
   - Click cell -> populates right-side detail column with prioritized suspects.

2) Quick Suspects list (top-right):
   - Ordered by combined signal: recent count * anomaly score * severity.
   - Suspect types: model-variant, routing-policy, region, quantization-profile, GPU-pool-id, customer-rate-limit.
   - Each suspect row shows small sparklines and one-click actions: "Open Trace", "Replay Sample", "Pin as hypothesis".

3) Request Replay tray (bottom):
   - Lightweight replay that can re-run a sanitized request against selected model variants (no PII).
   - Toggle options: attach KV cache snapshot, limit seq length, enable/disable batching.
   - Replay results: success / timeout / error + token-level timing breakdown.

4) Model Error Inspector modal:
   - For model-typed errors, surface: raw model error string, last logits snapshot (sanitized), tokenizer diagnostics (bad token indices), and memory utilization at time of error.
   - Quick suggestion lines (from heuristics): "Try shorter max_tokens", "Fallback to quantized variant", "Reduce batch size".

Wireframe notes (interaction + layout):
- Left column: time-range selector + high-level KPIs (p95 latency, error rate, qps).
- Center pane: Failure Journey Matrix (interactive heatmap). Hover shows top-3 sample requests for that cell.
- Right column: Quick Suspects + action buttons. Suspects expand inline to show supporting evidence (trace id list, histogram of latencies).
- Bottom dock: Replay / test panel that slides up and keeps context of selected sample.
- All items can be bookmarked to a "Triage Card" (small JSON snapshot) that can be attached to tickets.

Data fields to display per request sample (min viable):
- request_id, trace_id, timestamp, region, model_variant, model_revision, route, response_status, latency_ms, batch_size, cached_prefix_hit, gpu_pool_id, customer_id (hashed).
- Optional: tokens_generated, bytes_out, memory_used_mb.

Behavioral heuristics to rank suspects (server side):
- Spike score = z-score of count over 1h baseline + recency weight.
- Severity multiplier for model-error types (OOM > tokenization > unknown logits).
- Cross-signal correlation: region * model_variant co-occurrence.

Accessibility and performance notes:
- Colors: use colorblind-friendly palette for heatmap (avoid red/green).
- Ensure keyboard access to Quick Suspects rows and Replay actions.
- Lazy-load sample traces only when the suspect is expanded.

Backlog grooming (candidate tickets, rough priorities):
- P0: failure-journey-matrix-server-agg (compute 2D cell aggregates for last 30m/1h) - acceptance: API returns grid with counts and sample ids (DEV-1).
- P0: quick-suspects-ranking-api (expose ranked suspects per time-range) - acceptance: top-5 suspects include evidence links (trace ids) (DEV-2).
- P1: ui-heatmap-component (interactive heatmap with hover sample preview) - acceptance: hover shows 3 sample rows (UX-7).
- P1: replay-tray-minimal (server-side safe-replay + UI dock) - acceptance: can replay sample in sandbox without PII and return outcome (QA-11).
- P1: model-error-inspector (tokenizer + memory snapshot) - acceptance: displays sanitized tokenizer error and memory metric (ENG-45).
- P2: triage-card-bookmarking (save snapshot to paste in ticket) - acceptance: saved card includes suspect id + sample id (OPS-9).
- P3: accessibility-audit (keyboard + contrast) - acceptance: pass automated axe checks for main page (OPS-2).

Acceptance criteria (for first end-to-end prototype):
- Can identify and open detailed view for a heatmap cell showing timeout spikes in last 30 minutes.
- Quick Suspects list surfaces at least one correlated suspect with trace links.
- Replay of a sample returns a determinable outcome (success/timeout/error) and small timing breakdown.
- UI renders in <= 150ms for default 1h window (on staging).

Sketch / micro-prototypes (notes to designers):
- Sketch A: horizontal layout: heatmap center, suspects right, replay bottom dock. Emphasize density for power users.
- Sketch B: compact overlay: heatmap as mini-map; clicking expands to full-screen timeline for deep dives.
- Sketch C: incident-mode: when a severity threshold is hit, show first-time walkthrough overlay with suggested actions (replay, fallback to variant, create incident).

Edge cases and risks:
- Replay could expose sensitive prompt content. Mitigation: server-side sanitizer + customer opt-out flag.
- Over-aggregation hides noise; provide ability to drill into raw traces.
- Model errors may lack deterministic reproducibility (non-deterministic ops); annotate replays with confidence level.

Open questions (for next sync):
- How do we best represent batch contention vs single-request slowdowns in a single heatmap?
- Should suspects scoring incorporate customer SLA tiers (priority customers first)?
- Are there existing UX primitives in Console codebase we can reuse for the heatmap? (ask frontend infra).

Next steps and owners:
- Marisol: coordinate infra tickets for server-side aggregates (due 2026-03-10).
- Owen: prototype heatmap React component (initial PR by 2026-02-14).
- Priya: draft replay API contract w/ security review (draft by 2026-02-28).
- Ethan: run quick survey with 5 SREs to validate suspect ranking heuristic (results by 2026-03-01).

Notes from quick hallway sync (2026-02-20):
- SREs asked for "bookmarkable" state so they can attach to PagerDuty incidents.
- Two requests: show "last successful invocation" time for a model variant; and surface whether variant is using a progressive rollout.

Loose UX copy examples (for prototypes):
- Heatmap cell tooltip header: "Timeouts — 12 in last 30m (p95 1.8s)"
- Suspect action: "Open traces (5)" / "Replay sample" / "Pin hypothesis"
- Replay result status: "Replayed against v2-quant: TIMED_OUT (1.6s) — batch-size=4"

End of doc. This is intentionally exploratory; use as reference for grooming and initial frontend proof-of-concept.
